sections.title_da: What do you do? — Chno katkhdmi?
sections.body_da:
Bach tsewli chi wa7ed 3la khedmto, l'ingliz kay9oulo `What do you do?` — 7arfiyan "chno katdir?", walakin lma3na: chno katkhdem? Kayn 7ta `What's your job?`, nefs lma3na.

Ljawab: `I'm a` + lkhedma. Dima m3a `a` wla `an` (bhal dars 6): `I'm a nurse.`, `I'm an engineer.` — machi "I'm nurse".

Bach t9oli fin w kifach katkhdmi:

- `I work in` + lblassa: `I work in a hospital.` = kankhdem f sbitar.
- `I work for` + cherika wla chkhss: `I work for a big company.` = kankhdem 3nd cherika kbira.
- `I work as` + lkhedma: `I work as a cashier.` = kankhdem kaysiya.

W ila makatkhdmich daba: `I'm unemployed.` = makhddamach, wla `I'm looking for a job.` = kan9elleb 3la khedma. `I'm self-employed.` = kankhdem l rassi.

**Nasi7a:** `What do you do?` (lkhedma) machi bhal `What are you doing?` (chno katdiri daba — dars 13). Farra9i binathom!

sections.title_da: have to / don't have to — khassni / machi daroori
sections.body_da:
`have to` + lfi3l = khass + lfi3l: 7aja wajiba, lazem tdiriha (l9anoun, lkhedma, lmoudir…).

- `I have to work on Saturday.` = khassni nkhdem nhar ssebt.
- M3a `he/she/it`: `has to` → `She has to wear a uniform.` = khassha tlbes lebsa dyal lkhedma.
- So2al: `Do you have to…?` / `Does she have to…?` → `Yes, I do.` / `No, she doesn't.`
- Lmadi (dars 16): `had to` → `Yesterday I had to stay late.` = lbare7 kan khassni nb9a 7ta l m3ettel.

Nnafi: `don't have to` / `doesn't have to` = **machi daroori** — 3ndek lkhtiyar, ila ma dertihach 3adi.

- `We don't have to work on Sundays.` = makhassnach nkhdmo nhar l7edd (3ndna rra7a).
- `He doesn't have to wear a suit.` = machi daroori ylbes kostim.

Bhal f darija: "khassni" = `I have to`, "machi daroori" = `I don't have to`. Redi lbal: `don't have to` **machi** mamnou3! Mamnou3 ghadi nchoufouh f l9ism jjay m3a `mustn't`.

sections.body_da:
`must` = lazem — 9awiya chwiya kter men `have to`, kat9al f l9awanin, l'ichharat w l'awamir. `must` ma katbeddelch: `I must`, `she must` (bla `-s`), w men ba3dha lfi3l direct, bla `to`: `You must wear a helmet.` (machi "must to wear").

`mustn't` (= `must not`) = **mamnou3**: `You mustn't smoke here.` = mamnou3 tkemmi hna.

Lfar9 lmohimm:

- `You don't have to come.` = machi daroori tji (ila bghiti tji, mer7ba; ila la, 3adi).
- `You mustn't come.` = mamnou3 tji!

F lhadra l3adiya, l'ingliz kaysta3mlo `have to` kter men `must`. `must` kat9rayha bzzaf f lwra9 w l'ichharat: `Visitors must sign here.`

sections.title_da: Lmo9abala dyal lkhedma — the job interview
sections.body_da:
F `job interview` (lmo9abala dyal lkhedma), kaynin as2ila kaytsewlo dima. Wejjdi ljawab dyalek men 9bel!

- `Tell me about yourself.` = hder liya 3la rassek. → smiytek, l3mer, mnin nti, chno 9riti, fin khdemti: `My name is Nouha, I'm 28. I studied tourism and I worked as a receptionist for two years.`
- `Why do you want this job?` = 3lach bghiti had lkhedma? → `Because I like working with people.` / `Because I want to learn new things.`
- `What are your strengths?` = chno hiya no9at l9owwa dyalek? → `I'm organized, I'm patient and I work well in a team.`
- `Do you have experience?` = wach 3ndek tajriba? → `Yes, I have three years of experience as a receptionist.` / `No, but I learn fast.`

Lkelmat dyal `CV`: `experience` = ttajriba, `skills` = lmaharat (chno kat3rfi ddiri), `diploma` = ddiplom / chhada, `full-time` = b lwa9t kaml, `part-time` = b nos lwa9t, `salary` = chhriya.

Redi lbal: 3la lkhedma li fatet, sta3mli lmadi (dars 16): `I worked`, `I studied`. 3la daba: `I work`, `I'm working`.

reading.text_en:
Omar is 30 years old and he lives in Tangier. He works in a big car factory. He has to start work at seven o'clock in the morning, so he gets up at half past five. He must wear a uniform, a helmet and special shoes, because the factory can be dangerous. Omar works full-time, from Monday to Friday. He doesn't have to work at the weekend. He likes his colleagues, but the work is hard and the salary is not very high.

His sister Laila is a teacher. She works part-time in a primary school in Tetouan. She has to prepare her lessons at home, but she doesn't have to wear a uniform. Her students are small children, so she must be patient. Laila loves her job. Next month, she has an interview for a full-time job in a bigger school. She is a little nervous, but she has a diploma and five years of experience.
reading.text_da:
Omar 3ndo 30 3am w kayskon f Tanja. Kaykhdem f wa7ed lma3mel kbir dyal ttomobilat. Khasso ybda lkhedma m3a ssb3a dyal sbah, 3la hadak kayfi9 m3a lkhemsa w nos. Lazem ylbes lebsa dyal lkhedma, lkask w sbbat khass, 7it lma3mel y9der ykoun khatir. Omar kaykhdem b lwa9t kaml, men ttnin 7ta l jem3a. Makhassouch ykhdem f ssebt w l7edd. Kay3jbouh zmlano, walakin lkhedma s3iba w chhriya machi 3alya bzzaf.

Khto Laila oustada. Katkhdem b nos lwa9t f wa7ed lmedrasa ibtida2iya f Titwan. Khassha twejjed ddorous dyalha f ddar, walakin makhasshach tlbes lebsa dyal lkhedma. Ttlamed dyalha drari sghar, 3la hadak lazem tkoun sbbara. Laila kat3chi9 khdemtha. Chhar jjay, 3ndha mo9abala l khedma b lwa9t kaml f medrasa kber. Hiya mkhel3a chwiya, walakin 3ndha ddiplom w khemsa dyal ssnin dyal ttajriba.

sections.body_da:
`would like` = bghit, walakin b 'adab kter men `want`. `I would like` kat9esser dima w katwelli `I'd like`.

Kaynin jouj tari9at:

- `I'd like` + ism: `I'd like a ticket to London.` = bghit tikiya l London.
- `I'd like to` + fi3l: `I'd like to book a room.` = bghit n7jez bit.

So2al: `Would you like…?` = wach bghiti…? Ljawab: `Yes, please.` / `No, thank you.`

Katkhdem m3a ga3 nnas: `She'd like`, `We'd like`, `They'd like` — nefs lforma, bla `-s`.

F darija kan9oulo "bghit" f kolchi, walakin f lingliziya `I want a room` kat'ban 9ass7a chwiya m3a nnas li makat3rfihomch. F lotil, f lmatar, f restaurant → dima `I'd like`. (Chefti `I'd like` 9bel f dars 9, f l9ehwa — hna nefs chi, walakin f ssafar.)

- `Window or aisle?` = blassa 7da cherjem (`window seat`) wla 7da lmemcha (`aisle seat`)? Redi lbal: `aisle` kat9ra "aïl" — l `s` ma kat9rach!
- `security` = lmora9aba. `passport control` = lmora9aba dyal lpasspor.
- `gate` = lbab fin katrekbi ttiyara: `Gate 12`. `boarding` = rrkoub.
- `flight` = rri7la / ttiyara: `Is the flight on time?` = wach ttiyara f lwa9t? `The flight is delayed.` = ttiyara mt3ettla.

`luggage` (wla `baggage`) = lbagaj — ism ma kayt3eddch, bhal `water`: `my luggage is heavy` (machi "luggages"). Bach t3eddi: `one bag`, `two suitcases`. `hand luggage` = ssak sghir li kaydkhol m3ak f ttiyara.

Melli katwesli l lotil, kat9oli: `Hello, I have a reservation.` = 3ndi 7ajz, wla `I'd like to check in.`

- `check in` = kat'akhdi ssarout melli katwesli. `check out` = katkhelsi w katkhelli lbit melli katmchi. So2al mohimm: `What time is check-out?` (3adatan m3a l7dach wla ttnach).
- Nnaw3 dyal lbit: `single room` = bit l wa7ed, `double room` = bit l jouj (nmousiya kbira), `twin room` = bit b jouj nmousiyat.
- `Is breakfast included?` = wach lftor dakhel f ttaman?
- `key` / `key card` = ssarout / lkart dyal lbit. `floor` = ttab9a: `Your room is on the third floor.` (l'ar9am ttartibiya men dars 11: `first`, `second`, `third`).

Bach ttelbi chi 7aja b 'adab: `Could I have…, please?` → `Could I have the Wi-Fi password, please?`, `Could I have another towel?`. `Could I have` 'adab kter men `Can I have` (dars 9 w 14).

Ila kan chi mochkil, bdaï dima b 'adab: `Excuse me, there's a problem with my room.` Men ba3d 9oli chno lmochkil:

- `The Wi-Fi doesn't work.` = lWi-Fi makhddamch. (`doesn't work` = nnafi dyal l7adir lbassit, dars 8.) `The air conditioning doesn't work.` = lklimatizasyon makhddamach.
- `There's no hot water.` = makaynch lma skhoun. `There are no towels.` = makaynch lfwat. (`There's no` / `There are no` = dars 10.)
- `The room is too noisy.` = lbit fih ssda3 bzzaf. `It's too cold.` (`too` = bzzaf, kter men lma39oul — dars 12.)

Men ba3d, tlbi l7ell: `Could you send someone to fix it?` = wach ymken tsift chi wa7ed ysle7ha? wla `Could I change rooms?` = wach n9der nbeddel lbit?

Lmowaddaf ghadi yjawbek: `I'm sorry about that. I'll send someone right away.` = sme7 liya, ghadi nsift chi wa7ed daba daba. (`I'll` = 9arar f lwa9t, dars 19.)

At Casablanca airport, she went to the check-in desk, showed her passport and got her boarding pass. She asked for a window seat because she wanted to see the sea. The flight was delayed for one hour, so she drank a coffee and read a book. In Istanbul, she took a taxi to the hotel. She had a reservation for a single room for four nights, with breakfast included. The room was small but clean, and it was on the fifth floor, with a beautiful view of the city. On the first night, the Wi-Fi didn't work, so she went to the reception and asked politely for help. The receptionist was very kind and fixed the problem in ten minutes. Amina says it was the best trip of her life.

sections.title_da: F ttilifoun — kifach njawbo w n9eddmo rassna
sections.body_da:
F ttilifoun, lingliziya kattbeddel chwiya. Bach t9oli chkoun nti, **ma t9olich** `I'm Nouha` — 9oli: `Hello, this is Nouha.` wla `It's Nouha.` (`this is` hna = ana / hadi).

Bach tsewli chkoun kay3eyyet: `Who's calling, please?` = chkoun m3aya, 3afak?

Bach ttelbi chi wa7ed:

- `Can I speak to Sarah, please?` = wach ymken nhder m3a Sarah?
- `Could I speak to Mr. Brown, please?` — `Could` 'adab kter (f lkhedma, m3a nnas li makat3rfihomch).

Ljawab:

- `Speaking.` = ana hiya / ana howa (7arfiyan: "kanhder"). Kat9al melli nti bnefsek li kaytleb lik.
- `Hold on, please.` / `Just a moment, please.` = tsenna chwiya, 3afak.
- `I'll put you through.` = ghadi nwesslek (lih / liha).
- `Sorry, she's not here right now.` = sme7 liya, hiya makaynach daba. `He's in a meeting.` = rah f ijtima3.

Bhal f darija: "Allo, chkoun m3aya?" → `Hello, who's calling?`

Bach tsewli chi wa7ed makat3rfihch b 'adab, l'ingliz kaydiro so2al dakhel so2al:

- `Where is the bank?` → `Could you tell me where the bank is?` = wach ymken t9oul liya fin kayna lbanka?
- `Where is the bank?` → `Do you know where the bank is?` = wach kat3ref fin kayna lbanka?

**Redi lbal l ttartib:** men ba3d `Could you tell me…` / `Do you know…`, lfi3l kaymchi l **l'akhir**, bhal jomla 3adiya, machi bhal so2al: `where the bank is` (machi "where is the bank").

M3a l7adir lbassit, `do` / `does` kaytmse7: `What time does the shop open?` → `Do you know what time the shop opens?` (lfi3l kayakhod `-s`).

So2al dyal `wach` (`yes` / `no`) → kanzido `if`: `Is Sarah there?` → `Could you tell me if Sarah is there?`

F darija 3ndna nefs lfikra: "Wach t9der t9oul liya fin kayna lbanka?" — sahla 3lik!

`email` wla `message` 9sir 3ndo 4 ajza2:

**1. Tta7iya:** m3a s7ab: `Hi Sarah,` / `Hello Omar,`. Rasmi (lkhedma, l'idara): `Dear Mr. Brown,` / `Dear Ms. Alami,`. Ila makat3rfich smiyt chkhss: `Dear Sir or Madam,`.

**2. 3lach katktbi:** rasmi: `I'm writing to ask about…` = kanktb lik bach nsewwel 3la…, `I'm writing to confirm…` = bach n'akked… M3a s7ab: `Just a quick message to say…` = ghir `message` 9sir bach n9oul… W bach tchekri: `Thank you for your email / your help.`

**3. Ttalab:** `Could you send me…?` = wach ymken tsift liya…? / `Could you tell me if…?`

**4. Lkhtam:** rasmi: `Best regards,` / `Kind regards,` + smiytek. M3a s7ab: `See you soon!` / `Take care!` / `Love,` (ghir m3a l3a2ila w s7ab 9rab bzzaf).

F lmessajat m3a s7ab, kaynin ikhtisarat: `thx` = `thanks`, `pls` = `please`, `u` = `you`, `CU` = `see you`, `ASAP` = `as soon as possible` (f a9rab wa9t), `btw` = `by the way` (bilmonassaba). **Ma tsta3mlihomch f `email` rasmi!**

I look forward to meeting you.

Best regards,
David Brown

title_en: Have you ever…? Present perfect & big review
goals_da: Thedri 3la ttajarib dyal 7yatek b `have/has` + `past participle`: `I have been to Spain`
Tsewli w tjawbi 3la `Have you ever…?` b `Yes, I have` / `No, never`
Tferr9i bin `been` w `gone`, w bin `present perfect` w `past simple`
T3awdi l'ahamm no9at dyal A1 w A2: `to be`, `present simple`, `past simple`, `going to`, `comparatives`

sections.body_da:
Melli kanhedro 3la 7aja derniha f 7yatna **bla ma n9oulo fo9ach**, kansta3mlo `present perfect`: `have` / `has` + `past participle` (ttasrif ttalet dyal lfi3l).

- L'af3al l3adiya: `past participle` = nefs lforma dyal lmadi b `-ed`: `visited`, `tried`, `worked`.
- L'af3al li machi 3adiya (7fedihom!): `be → been`, `see → seen`, `eat → eaten`, `go → gone`, `meet → met`, `do → done`, `have → had`, `drink → drunk`, `read → read`, `write → written`, `take → taken`.

L'amtila: `I have visited Fes.` = zert Fes (f 7yati, chi merra — fo9ach? machi mohimm). `She has eaten sushi.` = hiya sb9 liha klat sushi.

L'ikhtisar: `I've`, `you've`, `we've`, `they've` / `he's`, `she's` (hna `'s` = `has`!).

Nnafi: `haven't` / `hasn't`: `I haven't seen that film.` = ma cheftch dak lfilm (7ta daba).

F darija kan9oulo "sb9 liya…" wla "3emmerni ma…": `I have tried couscous with fish.` = sb9 liya klit lkesksou b l7out.

sections.body_da:
`ever` = chi merra f 7yatek (kayji f so2al): `Have you ever been to Spain?` = wach 3emrek mchiti l Spanya?

Ljawab l9sir:

- `Yes, I have.` = ah, sb9 liya.
- `No, I haven't.` = la, 3emmerni.
- `No, never.` = la, 3emmerni (walou).

`never` = 3emmer… ma. Hiya b rassha nafiya, 3la hadak **ma kanzidouch** `not`: `I have never been to Spain.` (machi "I haven't never").

M3a `he/she`: `Has she ever…?` → `Yes, she has.` / `No, she hasn't.`

`been to` = mchit l (w rje3t): `I've been to Spain.` Dima m3a `to`: `been to Spain`, `been to the cinema`.

Bhal f darija: "Wach 3emrek…?" → "3emmerni!" wla "Ah, sb9 liya." Sahla, yak?

sections.title_da: been wla gone? Present perfect wla past simple?
sections.body_da:
**`been` wla `gone`?**

- `She has been to London.` = mchat l London w rej3at (ttajriba).
- `She has gone to London.` = mchat l London w **mazal temma** (makaynach daba).

**`present perfect` wla `past simple`?**

- `present perfect` = ttajriba, **bla wa9t m7edded**: `I have visited Fes.` (fo9ach? ma mohimch).
- `past simple` (dars 15-16) = m3a **wa9t m7edded**: `I visited Fes last year.`, `in 2020`, `yesterday`, `two days ago`, `when I was a child`.

F lhadra, 3adatan kanbdaw b `present perfect` w kankemmlo b `past simple`:

`Have you ever been to Marrakech?` → `Yes, I have. I went there last summer. It was great!`

**L9a3ida ddahabiya:** ila kayna `yesterday`, `last…`, `…ago`, `in 2015`, `when…` → `past simple`, **3emmerk** ma tsta3mli `present perfect`!

sections.body_da:
Mabrouk, Nouha! Hada l'akhir dars. Nchoufo l'ahamm no9at f jomla wa7da kol wa7da:

- `to be` (dars 3): `am / is / are` → `I'm a nurse.`, `She isn't here.`, `Are you ready?`
- `present simple` (dars 7-8): l3adat w l7a9ayi9 → `I work`, `she works`, `Do you…?`, `Does she…?`, `don't / doesn't`.
- `present continuous` (dars 13): daba → `I'm studying now.`
- `past simple` (dars 15-16): lmadi m7edded → `was / were`, `went`, `didn't go`, `Did you go?`
- Lmosta9bal (dars 19): `going to` l lmokhattat → `I'm going to travel.` / `will` l l9arar w lwa3d → `I'll help you.`
- Lmo9arana (dars 20): `bigger than`, `more expensive than`, `the best`.
- `have to / must` (dars 21), `I'd like` (dars 22), `Could you tell me…?` (dars 23).
- `present perfect` (dars 24): ttajarib → `Have you ever…?`

**L7ila:** sewli rassek **fo9ach?** → daba (`continuous`), dima (`simple`), lbare7 (`past`), ghedda (`going to` / `will`), f 7yati bla wa9t (`present perfect`).

sections.body_da: Melli katsewli `Have you ever…?`, ljawab l9sir kafi: `Yes, I have.` / `No, never.` W men ba3d, ila bghiti tzidi ttafasil (fo9ach? fin? m3a men?) — dowzi l lmadi lbassit: `I went there in 2019.` Hadi hiya l9a3ida ddahabiya: ttajriba → `present perfect`; lwa9t m7edded → `past simple`. W mabrouk, Nouha — hada l'akhir dars! Mchiti men `Hello` 7ta l `Have you ever…?`. 3awdi ddorous li s3ab 3lik, w kemmli ttari9!

reading.text_en: My name is Amina and I'm 35 years old. I have had a very interesting life. I was born in a small village near Ouarzazate, but I moved to Marrakech in 2010. I have worked as a nurse, a tour guide and, today, an English teacher. I have travelled a lot: I've been to France, Turkey and Egypt, and I've visited twelve Moroccan cities. I've never been to America, but I'm going to go next year, because my sister lives in New York. I've eaten strange food in my life: snails in Jemaa el-Fna and raw fish in Istanbul. But I've never tried camel meat! I've met many kind people, and I've learned three languages. Last month, I started my fourth: Spanish. It's harder than English, but it's more useful for my job. My advice? Life is short. Try new things, visit new places and never stop learning.
reading.text_da: Smiyti Amina w 3ndi 35 3am. 3echt 7ayat mohimma bzzaf. Tzadit f wa7ed ddouwar sghir 7da Werzazat, walakin nta9elt l Marrakech f 2010. Khdemt fermliya, w morchida siya7iya, w lyouma oustada dyal lingliziya. Saffert bzzaf: mchit l Fransa, Torkya w Masr, w zert tnach mdina meghribiya. 3emmerni ma mchit l Amrika, walakin ghadi nmchi l3am jjay, 7it khti kateskon f New York. Klit makla ghriba f 7yati: lbebbouch f Jam3 lfna w l7out khder f Istanbul. Walakin 3emmerni ma jerrebt l7em jjmel! Tla9it bzzaf dyal nnas dérifin, w t3ellemt tlata dyal lloghat. Chhar li fat, bdit rrab3a: l'isbaniya. S3iba kter men lingliziya, walakin nafi3a kter l khdemti. Nnasi7a dyali? L7ayat 9sira. Jerrbi 7wayj jdad, zouri blayes jdad w 3emmrek ma t7ebsi tt3ellem.

writing.model_en: I'm Nouha and I've had many good experiences in my life. I've been to Spain twice, with my family. The first time was in 2018, and we visited Madrid. I've visited many cities in Morocco, but I've never been to the Sahara. I've eaten pizza, sushi and Turkish food, and I've tried snails in Marrakech.
